iconicAnchor.label: Fluent Acrylic interface material
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Microsoft's Acrylic material explicitly combines translucency, background blur, tint, texture, and contrast to establish depth and hierarchy on functional interface surfaces.

sources.title: Acrylic material
supports: Acrylic uses translucency, blur, noise, tint, and blending to add depth and establish interface hierarchy.
The guidance limits acrylic to appropriate surfaces, warns against stacked layers, and requires legible foreground content.

sources.title: Materials
supports: Interface materials use blur, vibrancy, and blending to separate foreground controls from background content while preserving context.
Material thickness and contrast must be selected for semantic purpose and foreground legibility, not color effect alone.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches interface signal, digital signal, screen scale, translucent, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/glassmorphism/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
